ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, directors, prescribed officers, and authorized signatories against the South African terrorist and related-activities list (POCDATARA s.25), the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, the OFAC SDN list, the EU consolidated list, and the African Union Union list; enhanced due diligence for foreign and domestic PEPs under FICA ss.21F and 21G; verification of source of funds and source of wealth for all SWIFT wire and letter-of-credit payment rails; ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening (at least annually) commensurate with the Medium_Risk_Enhanced classification of the ISIC 2720 sodium-ion battery cell manufacturing scope.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services portal — https://eservices.cipc.co.za (name reservation and incorporation via registered CIPC agents or direct online submission)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A company name may be in any of South Africa's 11 official languages but must be rendered in Latin script for CIPC database capture; names consisting solely of symbols or unsupported characters are rejected; foreign-language names must be accompanied by a sworn transliteration or translation declaration; the name must not be undesirably offensive, misleading, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or trademark.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon CIPC refusal, the applicant receives a notice of refusal with reasons; the applicant may file written representations under s.13(4) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 within 20 business days of the notice. If CIPC confirms the refusal, the applicant may apply to the Companies Tribunal for administrative review under s.160 using Form CTR 142 within 6 months of the refusal. A rejected applicant may alternatively file a fresh name reservation application (current statutory fee ZAR 50) or seek urgent High Court relief if the refusal is manifestly unlawful or procedurally unfair; the CIPC decision does not suspend parallel reservation of an amended alternative name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted as a registered service address only if a physical street address located in South Africa is provided to CIPC; a PO Box alone is statutorily insufficient. A virtual/co-working registered office satisfies CIPC and SARS address requirements, but the accepting bank will typically require a physical operating-site verification within 6 months of account opening, and the CIPC UBO register filings require a residential or business address that must be verifiable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium–High (approximately 35% probability within the first 24 months). Likely inspection triggers: SARS VAT and income-tax on-site verification campaigns; Department of Employment and Labour workplace inspections; NEMA environmental-authorization compliance monitoring by the provincial environmental department; municipal business-license audits; and bank site visits for a Medium_Risk_Enhanced manufacturing entity using SWIFT and letter-of-credit rails.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up or authorised share capital is prescribed for a private company under the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Shares may be issued with a nil or nominal par value; no escrow account or capital deposit rule applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) e-Services Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application on Form CoR 9.1 through the CIPC e-Services portal after conducting a name search against the CIPC register. Pay the prescribed reservation fee electronically. The reserved name is valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Copy of applicant's certified identity document or passport
Payment receipt for name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, lodge a fresh CoR 9.1 application with an alternative unique name and pay the applicable fee. A refusal notice may be challenged by written representation to CIPC within 10 business days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and file the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (CoR 15.1B), executed by each incorporator. Attach the notice of registered office and director consents. Pay the registration fee online. CIPC will issue a unique enterprise registration number upon successful lodgement.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director forms (CoR 14.2)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, correct the identified deficiency and resubmit through the CIPC Query and Resubmission facility within 20 business days. Re-execution of the CoR 14.1 by all incorporators is required for any material amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Registration Certificate and Company File Establishment
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, CIPC issues the Registration Certificate (CoR 14.3) and establishes the company file. Verify the correctness of company name, registration number, date, and registered address. Download and retain the certified MOI and certificate as definitive legal records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains administrative errors, apply to CIPC for rectification under section 23(3) of the Companies Act, filing a notice of correction with supporting affidavits and the original certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) eFiling; Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, VAT, PAYE, UIF, and SDL via SARS eFiling using the registration certificate and MOI. Obtain a tax compliance status pin. Register the company as an accountable institution with the FIC to enable SWIFT wire and letter-of-credit banking facilities.
required_dossiers: Certified ID copies of directors and beneficial owners
Bank letter confirming settlement account details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects the registration, resubmit through a SARS branch with certified documents and a covering letter explaining the discrepancy. For FIC issues, file a correction or confirmation application within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial and Manufacturing Operating Licence Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS); South African Bureau of Standards (SABS); Department of Employment and Labour
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for a manufacturing operating clearance covering the assembly of sodium-ion energy cells for micro-mobility. Provide an OHS risk assessment, process flow diagrams, chemical storage inventory, and emergency response plan. Undergo the mandatory NRCS/SABS inspection of the production facility before commencing commercial production.
required_dossiers: Hazardous chemical and waste management plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the operating licence is refused, file an appeal with the relevant provincial Department of Employment and Labour within 30 days. Rectify all non-conformances identified in the inspection report and apply for a reinspection prior to appeal determination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental Impact Assessment and Civil Defence Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE); Local Municipal Building Control and Fire Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Commission a registered Environmental Assessment Practitioner to undertake the scoping and environmental impact report under the 2014 EIA Regulations. Apply for a water use licence under the National Water Act if wastewater discharge or water abstraction exceeds thresholds. Submit building plans to the municipality for structural, fire, and occupational safety clearance prior to production commencement.
required_dossiers: EIA scoping report and environmental impact report
Fire safety compliance certificate under SANS 10400
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EIA is refused, pursue an appeal under section 43 of the National Environmental Management Act within 60 days of written notice. For municipal plan rejections, correct the specified plan deviations and resubmit through the local municipality planning department.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); national e-portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.efiling.gov.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity deriving South African source income or carrying on an enterprise in South Africa must first be registered as a taxpayer with SARS. The practical sequence is: (1) incorporate at the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) or register the foreign company as an external company; (2) obtain an income tax reference number through SARS eFiling or by appointment at a SARS branch, using the relevant non-resident registration forms and supporting constitutional documents; (3) if taxable supplies exceed or are reasonably expected to exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in a consecutive 12-month period, apply for VAT vendor registration within 21 days of reaching the threshold; (4) obtain the statutory tax clearance status / vendor number relevant to the activity. SARS accepts registration through a registered tax practitioner or via direct eFiling non-resident taxpayer portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box classification regime. A private company (Pty Ltd) is taxed at entity level as a 'taxpayer' under the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962. Relevant statutory elections include: VAT grouping of two or more persons as one vendor under section 50 of the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991; corporate reorganisation rollover relief elections under sections 45, 47, 48 and 55 of the Income Tax Act; CFC inclusion elections; and hybrid mismatch arrangements subject to specific anti-avoidance provisions, with no free election to disregard the domestic corporate entity for tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: ZAR 1,000,000 taxable supplies in a consecutive 12-month period, measured on a rolling basis; registration compulsory within 21 days once the threshold is reached or can reasonably be expected to be reached.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: There is no mandatory real-time national electronic invoice clearance or digital stamping framework in South Africa. VAT vendors must issue full South African tax invoices meeting section 20 VAT Act content requirements; returns and reconciliations are submitted via SARS eFiling with prescribed deadlines. SARS may require electronic communication and automated data reporting for registered vendors, but there is no continuous transaction control (CTC) clearance API requirement in force.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The export and supply of goods physically removed from South Africa to a non-resident are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act if goods are exported under customs supervision and the supplier retains documentary proof of export. Related services physically rendered for the use of a non-resident outside South Africa, and supplies of certain movable goods supplied to non-residents for export, may also qualify for zero rating. The taxpayer must be a registered vendor and must hold documentary evidence before claiming zero-rating on the VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD 500 / SARS Customs entry with export clearance approval)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing physical export movement from South Africa
Commercial invoice / tax invoice with the zero-rating basis stated
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or authorised dealer foreign currency receipt statement
Shipping records, packing list, and proof of delivery to the non-resident consignee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are selected for higher-risk SARS verification where export evidence is incomplete or the 180-day foreign-currency remittance condition is not met. If documentary proof is absent or the goods were not physically exported, SARS will claw back the VAT at 15% and may impose a section 222 understatement penalty under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 of up to 125% of the shortfall, plus statutory interest and late/non-payment penalties. Deliberate submission of false or fraudulent export declarations may lead to criminal prosecution, monetary penalties, and in the case of exchange-control non-repatriation, additional SARB penalties and possible disqualification of preferential export treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), which administers exchange control under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations issued thereunder; regulation is delegated operationally to Authorized Dealers in foreign exchange (the commercial banks).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR, ZAR code 710) is classified as a managed-float currency with full current-account convertibility for merchandise trade, service fees, royalties, dividends and capital gains repatriation, subject to prescribed documentary vetting by an Authorized Dealer. Capital-account convertibility is restricted: inward foreign direct investment requires the submission of a Financial Liability Statement and the allocation of a 'non-resident' nodal reference by the receiving Authorized Dealer, while outward capital flows (loan redemptions, share buybacks, disinvestment) require FinSurv approval, SARS tax clearance certification, and the filing of Forms A1/A2 where applicable. Profit remittance (dividends) to non-resident shareholders is permitted without FinSurv pre-approval only if the company has a valid SARS Statement of Assets and Liabilities / Income and Capital Gains Tax clearance (tax compliance status PIN) and the dividend distribution is effected by an Authorized Dealer with appropriate balance-of-payments coding; withholding tax on dividends (20% now 10% subject to double taxation treaty relief) must be deducted and remitted to SARS before the net proceeds leave South Africa.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current SARS/SARB exchange control dispensation, all export proceeds from the manufacture and sale of sodium-ion battery cells must be repatriated to South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment unless an extension is granted by an Authorized Dealer or FinSurv (circulars allow 360 days for capital goods and project-based exports on application). There is no fixed statutory percentage conversion ratio; however, 100% of export value must be submitted for conversion or credited to a SARS/SARB-approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) maintained with an Authorized Dealer, with any material deviation from declared value requiring a pricing audit and supporting commercial documentation (invoice, packing list, bill of lading, customs SAD500 entry). For settlement, export proceeds may be retained in a specified FCA only for legitimate working-capital purposes, but any utilization must comply with the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual and be reported through the Authorized Dealer's exchange-control returns.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Feasibility / Supplementary Rail Only: Offshore digital financial services providers (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Currencycloud) may lawfully service the entity for inbound collections and outbound settlement in non-ZAR currencies, but they are not licensed Authorized Dealers in foreign exchange under SARB rules, cannot maintain a ZAR domestic account with SAMOS settlement access, and cannot legally facilitate the conversion or repatriation of export proceeds in ZAR unless they partner with a locally licensed Authorized Dealer. Consequently, such EMIs are a valid supplementary clearing channel for multi-currency receipts in USD/EUR for working-capital efficiency, but the primary banking relationship, statutory reporting, nodal allocation, LC issuing and tax-linked forex approvals must remain with a Tier-1 South African commercial bank; using an unlicensed EMI as principal rail creates a regulatory violation risk under the Financial Sector Regulation Act and exchange control regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical presence or dual-control video interview is effectively mandatory at the Tier-1 South African banks for a foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd. In practice, all banks operating under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) require the submission of certified copies of director passports, a board resolution, the Memorandum of Incorporation, CIPC certificate, and audited financial statements where applicable. Standard Bank, FNB and Absa will generally require at least one executive director or the company secretary to attend an in-person or bank-approved digital KYC interview (with presenters producing original ID/passport and a sworn/commissioner-of-oaths signature), while complete remote onboarding is normally rejected for entities with non-resident shareholders absent a strong existing international banking reference. Adequate economic substance (rented offices, payroll, SARS registration, local tax compliance) materially shortens the interview cycle and is the decisive test for account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident 100% ownership with no verifiable local business substance; bank perceives a letterbox-company structure for treasury migration or invoice redirection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC Certificate of Incorporation and latest Annual Return; signed lease agreement for South African registered office and production facility; SARS Income Tax and PAYE/UIF/SDL registration confirmations (tax PIN); three months of local payroll and utility invoices; board minutes evidencing local management control; supplier and off-take agreements naming ZA_PTY_LTD as principal manufacturer; notarized passports of directors and utility bills.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-based flag: battery cell manufacturing triggers dual-use or hazardous-material screening protocols under the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) higher-risk standards (chemical precursors, lithium/sodium process inputs, scrap metal exports).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original or certified import permits for sodium compounds, aluminium foil, electrolyte solvents, and separator materials; South African Bureau of Standards (SABS) test certificates and NEMA environmental compliance documentation; storage/safety permits from local municipality and Department of Employment and Labour; supplier due-diligence questionnaire and ISO 9001 / ISO 14001 certifications; detailed bill of materials mapping every input to the cell production line and confirming no dual-use end user.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection (share subscription) without clear source-of-funds trail and without allocated nodal reference, triggering unusual activity reports (STR/SAR) on the escrow account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution allotting shares in ZA_PTY_LTD to non-resident shareholders; executed share subscription agreement with stated consideration; signed source-of-funds declarations and six months of foreign bank statements from the investing entities/individuals; notarized UBO register and group structure chart; the SARB inward transfer nodal reference and FIN127/FIN150 correspondence from the Authorized Dealer; entity-level tax clearance PIN from SARS confirming no dispute with the fiscus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to/from higher-risk corridors (China for active anode materials, DRC for cobalt/sodium feed, UAE as a trade hub) triggering jurisdiction-risk reviews and potential 314(b) treatment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full KYC file of each overseas counterparty (certificate of incorporation, passports, license, complete bank details); commercial invoices with precise Incoterms, unit price breakdowns, HS codes; transport documentation (bill of lading, airway bill, customs SAD500); forward purchase agreements with supply chain validation; sanctions screening results confirming no SDN/OFAC or EU-restricted entities; compliance attestation letter signed by both buyer and seller stating beneficial ownership and absence of terrorist finance linkage.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing requires an international SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank to the beneficiary account of ZA_PTY_LTD held with the South African Authorized Dealer, with Field 50K (ordering customer), Field 57A (South African receiving bank with SARB authorization) and Field 70/72 (remittance information) quoting the BOP purpose code for inward direct investment in equity (Balance of Payments code FX2/EQ or the bank-specific Form A1 inward-share allocation). The shareholder must transmit a signed Financial Liability Statement (Form FLS) or written instruction confirming the funds are a capital contribution; the receiving bank will allocate a unique non-resident nodal reference and issue the company an Excon 'inward capital' acknowledgement; funds are credited to a Capital Escrow Account (non-resident nodar) and can only be released for operational expenditure once the bank verifies the share allotment resolution, the SARS entity tax PIN, and the absence of funds from a sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction. Loans instead of equity are discouraged: a cross-border shareholder loan requires FinSurv approval and SARS debt-to-equity thin-capitalization assessment before interest and principal may be serviced.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for imported anode/cathode materials, electrolyte and cell components are cleared through direct SWIFT MT103 payments from the operational ZAR/USD account for approved invoices under US$100,000, and through irrevocable confirmed Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP600) for bulk procurement over USD 100,000 or for first-transaction counterparties. For export receivables, the entity must obtain 100% of proceeds within 180 days; payment may be received by wire transfer, by documentary collection (D/P, D/A), or by sight/term LC issued in the company's favor; all receipts must be allocated to the Authorized Dealer's export control system and disposed of within the prescribed timeline. Internally, the company may establish a shared-service centre in South Africa that sweeps surplus liquidity into overnight call accounts or money-market funds via the bank's SAMOS EFT integration only for domestic ZAR flows, while all cross-border flows must remain in SWIFT and be recorded under the Excon reporting framework.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward exchange contracts (FECs) in USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR concluded exclusively through an Authorized Dealer, requiring documentary evidence of transactional exposure (binding purchase orders, sales contracts or approved investment timelines).

Cross-currency swaps (USD/ZAR and EUR/ZAR principal and interest exchange) executed with a SARB-regulated South African bank under an ISDA or local SEMA master agreement, subject to FinSurv approval and an economic-exposure statement.

Vanilla FX options (call and put structures) in USD/ZAR for asymmetric hedging of export receipts, purchased through an Authorized Dealer with the premium settled in ZAR and full TCF conduct documentation.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with offshore counterparties referencing USD/ZAR, permitted only as a hedge of genuine non-ZAR commercial exposure when the offshore counterparty cannot provide physical settlement in ZAR; the hedge must be documented via the South African Authorized Dealer and supported by exposure calculation worksheets to avoid speculative-trading characterization.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (AR) for a (Pty) Ltd private company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation each year; the filing window opens on the correspondence/filing date and closes on the last business day of the 30-business-day period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a penalty equal to double the standard annual return fee (approx. ZAR 1,150); continued non-filing for two consecutive return periods triggers a CIPC default notice and may lead to administrative deregistration under section 82(4) of the Companies Act, after which the company loses legal capacity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (BO) Declaration and Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be included with and confirmed in the annual return, i.e., within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary; any change in beneficial ownership during the year must be filed separately within 5 business days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-submission or inaccurate confirmation is an offence; CIPC may impose an administrative penalty of up to ZAR 1 million and directors/officers may be personally liable. Persistent non-compliance can block annual return acceptance and accelerate deregistration proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Maintained statutory register pack (Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Beneficial Ownership, Minute Book) available for inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuous maintenance obligation; registers must be updated within 5 business days of any relevant change and held at the registered office or another location approved by CIPC; no separate annual filing deadline, but CIPC may inspect at any time.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to keep or produce the statutory registers constitutes a contravention of the Companies Act; CIPC may impose an administrative fine, issue a compliance notice, and negative compliance status may prevent the annual return from being processed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private company must be audited if its Public Interest Score is 500 or above; if the score is between 100 and 499, an independent review is required unless voluntary audit is elected; if the score is below 100, no audit or independent review is mandatory. Public and state-owned companies are always subject to a compulsory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB or IFRS for SMEs as permitted by the Companies Act, 2008 and its Regulations; no separate South African local GAAP is available.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must keep a Register of Beneficial Ownership at its registered office, record all changes, and lodge a BO declaration with CIPC within 5 business days of any shareholding or control change. Each year, the CIPC Annual Return must include a confirmation that the BO register and filed declarations are accurate and up to date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Memorandum of Incorporation and special resolutions
Minute Book (shareholders, board and committee minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 55 - USD 195 per year (typical CIPC registered office and company secretarial agent fee in South Africa)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 8,500 per audit for a mid-size manufacturing (Pty) Ltd, depending on turnover, transactions, and group complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for companies with a year of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (previously 28%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 12C accelerated manufacturing capital allowance (40% first-year deduction, 20% per annum on manufacturing plant and machinery); Section 12B renewable-energy allowance (100% first-year deduction for qualifying battery storage assets, relevant to sodium-ion energy storage applications); Section 11D research and development deduction (150% deduction for SARS-approved sodium-ion chemistry R&D); Section 12I industrial investment allowance (up to 135% deduction for eligible greenfield or brownfield strategic projects); potential Small Business Corporation relief is not applicable because the entity is a standard (Pty) Ltd earning manufacturing income above the lower turnover threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 – Annual South African Corporate Income Tax Return, filed exclusively through the SARS eFiling portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (one return per year of assessment)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year / year of assessment; SARS may prescribe an earlier eFiling deadline by annual tax-season notice. For a 31 March year-end, the filing season is typically announced around August of the following year. Late filing triggers an estimated assessment under s95 TAA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year of assessment identifier (e.g., 2025 for a year of assessment ended 28 February or 31 March 2025).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the South African subsidiary's domestic financial year only; do not adopt the foreign parent's consolidated fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SARS income tax reference number and Companies Act registration number of the (Pty) Ltd.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent must register the entity through CIPC and SARS, appointing a local SARS-compliant tax representative where no resident director is in place.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial year-end date and period covered by the annual financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the tax return with the South African statutory financial statements; a group consolidated account submission is not acceptable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address, business address, and SARS correspondence contact.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide a physical South African address for service of SARS notices and appoint a local representative taxpayer in terms of s157 TAA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income, including gross manufacturing receipts from sodium-ion battery cell sales, by-products, scrap disposals, and related service income, adjusted for any transfer-pricing adjustment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All connected-party export sales must be invoiced at arm's length; contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation should support the gross income reflected.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income, including qualifying foreign dividends, s10(1)(h) interest, and other statutory exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exemptions are claimable only where the South African entity is the legal recipient and documentary proof of source and beneficial ownership is retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenditure added back, including capital outlays, fines, penalties, bribes, private expenses, non-commercial payments, and GAAR-tainted group charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deny any head-office management or license fee lacking economic substance; false add-back deductions can attract an understatement penalty of 100%-200%.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit or loss before capital allowances, special deductions, and assessed loss set-off.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Present actual South African operating data; head-office cost allocations must be charged at cost with evidence of benefit to the local manufacturing operation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward from prior years of assessment, subject to s20A change-of-ownership limitations and the 5-year carry-forward window.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A change of ultimate beneficial ownership may extinguish the loss unless the same trade continues and the loss was not acquired as a tax-trading tool.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or taxable loss after deducting allowances and setting off the assessed loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned manufacturer, taxable income must include all South African-source profits attributable to a domestic permanent establishment; treaty PE thresholds apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss carried forward to the next year of assessment; under this Stage 6 tax model, any residual unabsorbed loss expires after 5 years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses cannot be permanently warehoused in the South African subsidiary while connected foreign distributors report the corresponding profitable margins.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Normal corporate income tax computed at 27% on the taxable income before rebates and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The ITR14 does not provide credit for shareholder-level taxes in the parent jurisdiction; such relief is available via DTA foreign-tax-credit mechanisms at the parent level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits, rebates, and special deductions, including s12C/s12B capital allowances, the s11D R&D deduction, and s6quat foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the SARS-approved s11D project certificate and the capital allowance depreciation schedule; avoid claiming the same asset base through two group entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net normal tax payable or refundable after provisional tax credits, withholding credits, and the SARS reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settle the final balance within the prescribed period before declaring any dividend to the foreign parent; unpaid normal tax blocks the dividend route and triggers DWT liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 (TAA): an administrative non-compliance penalty of up to R250 per month (or, where turnover exceeds the threshold, an amount based on 0.5% of assessed tax per month, capped at 100% of the tax assessed); SARS is authorised to issue an estimated assessment under s95 TAA when the return is not filed; an understatement penalty of 10%-200% under s223 TAA applies where the eventual assessment exceeds the declared amount; statutory interest at the prescribed rate (approximately 10.5% per annum, adjusted quarterly) compounds daily on the outstanding balance; criminal prosecution for repeated non-filing is possible under s235 TAA.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IRP6 – Provisional Tax Return and Estimate, filed through SARS eFiling
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Semi-annual (two compulsory provisional estimates per year of assessment for companies)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: First provisional estimate and payment due within six months of the start of the year of assessment; second provisional estimate and payment due on or before the last day of the financial year; a third voluntary 'top-up' estimate may be submitted after financial statements are finalised, subject to SARS-prescribed due dates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Estimate of total taxable income for the full year, with payment of the first half of the estimated normal tax, submitted within the first six months of the year of assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base the estimate on the local manufacturing operating budget; intercompany back-charge income must be included at the arm's-length amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Updated estimate filed at the financial year-end reflecting actual full-year expectations, with the second half of the estimated tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for realised export volumes and final transfer-pricing adjustments; a low second estimate after a strong overseas sales quarter triggers the 20% underestimation penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Optional third estimate submitted once the annual financial statements are finalised, intended to reduce interest exposure on the difference between the second estimate and the final assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the top-up estimate with the audited local financial statements; the non-resident group auditor's consolidation figures are insufficient without a South African tax computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: IRP6 – Payment Reference and Credit Utilisation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provisional tax payment reference codes (PAY-1 and PAY-2) matched to the SARS taxpayer profile and prior-year credit balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain proof of payment from a South African bank account; overseas-sourced wire settlements require prior SARS forex authorisation and are otherwise treated as unpaid.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under s225 TAA a 20% penalty is imposed on the amount by which the provisional tax actually paid is less than the 'qualifying amount' where underestimation exceeds R20,000; the penalty may be waived only where the estimate was based on an honest and reasonable calculation; prescribed-rate interest is charged from the original provisional payment date until the final assessment; failure to submit the IRP6 additionally attracts the s210/s211 administrative non-compliance penalty and SARS may issue an estimate of taxable income.
